items.title: These weeks at Open Robotics HQ (since pre-ROSCon Global)
items.summary: Did I say I’d publish one of these right after ROSCon Global? I was overly ambitious (so, so overly ambitious). Truth be told, Open Robotics HQ is still digging out from all the good stuff that happened in Toronto. There’s a whole lot involved with tying off an event, not least of which are the dozens of follow-up conversations that started while in Toronto. We’re closing the loop on a lot of community questions, including how you can help and contribute more to our work, what it would look like if you joined the OSRA, how we can help you better engage with the community, how you can organize a local event, and more. ROSCon Global always happens right around the transition between Q3 and Q4 for the year. This means that aside from tying off matters from the event we also need to close out a quarter and prep for the next one. Q4 is always special (read: hectic!), because it includes working to wrap up one year while also setting the scene for another successful year to follow. Which is to say, there’s an awful lot of planning, organizing, and prioritizing happening and that takes way more time than you’d expect. There is also a bunch of local ROSCons coming up; there are six of them

Which is to say, there’s an awful lot of planning, organizing, and prioritizing happening and that takes way more time than you’d expect. There is also a bunch of local ROSCons coming up; there are six of them just in the last three months of the year. The local teams do most of the heavy lifting (thank you!), but it all still requires a lot of coordination here in HQ. Of course, the plans we made earlier in the year are still moving forward, so we’re fitting those tasks in there. We’re working on building partnerships with other open source organizations, and investigating how we can work with some academic institutions. There’s also the standing TGC meeting coming up next week, which always requires a lot of preparation. We have some really good stuff on the agenda, though, so keep an eye out for those meeting minutes! And, naturally, the yearly audit continues its crawl toward completion. Still. This may all sound a bit vague, but that’s a necessary evil. If I listed out everything that’s happened since before ROSCon Global y’all could just read this post to your kids to get them to sleep instead of singing a lullaby. items.summary: Some updates on ros2_pulse since the first post (Ros2_pulse: per-topic rates and node liveness, including intra-process, on stock binaries ), the LD_PRELOAD probe that counts per-topic rates and node liveness from the tracetools hooks instead of subscribing. Python nodes are counted on both sides now. Before, a Python subscriber’s deliveries never showed up, because rclpy isn’t instrumented. The Monitor’s built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server connects an MCP-compatible AI assistant to the system information and operations available in the Monitor. You can ask questions about the running system and inspect the resulting entities, charts and operations in the workspace. Investigate a communication problem using endpoint configuration, including a reliability QoS mismatch. Publish sample data to a selected topic in a test environment and observe the response. For ROS 2 deployments using DDS, the connection is the underlying DDS topics and endpoints. The Monitor works at that layer; this is not a claim that it understands every ROS graph concept or supports every ROS middleware implementation. Fast DDS Pro can also be integrated into ROS 2 and Vulcanexus to provide additional communication capabilities and professional tools. For a specific ROS 2 setup, compatibility and the available operations depend on the middleware, versions, topic type information and configuration. DDS Monitor Pro is a commercial product. These new capabilities are in final testing, with release expected in the coming weeks. The MCP server starts disabled. Once enabled, connected clients can invoke supported operations without a separate approval prompt for each action, so use trusted clients and a test environment for publishing data. items.title: Anthropic's Scion is heavily inspired by Mononoke
items.articleText: Anthropic's Scion is heavily inspired by Mononoke · sunshowers Anthropic’s Scion is heavily inspired by Mononoke 2026-10-14 · 2 min read vcs shorts Discuss on Hacker News or Lobsters . Here is Anthropic describing (archive link ) yesterday how their new version control system, Scion, uses a concept called “derived data” to make operations like blames more efficient: How Anthropic describes Scion’s derived data. Here is me, back in 2022, describing in my Oxide candidate materials how the Mononoke source control server I helped build uses a concept called “derived data” to make operations like blames more efficient: How I described Mononoke’s derived data. I think the level of imitation goes well beyond having similar insights1 . The fact that Sapling was only credited for “hard-won lessons”, and that Mononoke was not mentioned at all, borders on plagiarism. The post comes off as Anthropic claiming that Claude designed all this, while the reality is that our (extraordinary) team at Meta came up with many of the insights that Claude dutifully applied almost a decade later. (We looked at plenty of prior art for Mononoke and Sapling too, from Google’s SrcFS to write-ahead logs in databases.) I am very glad that the vision our team had back in 2017-18 was so powerful and enduring — when you go against the grain, you’re always a bit unsure if what you’re doing is genius or madness, and I think Mononoke’s design has stood the test of time. And, to be clear, I do not have a problem with Anthropic copying Mononoke’s design. (This is part of why we put out open source — to benefit humanity through the spread of good ideas.) But as LLMs continue to assist in designing new systems, they are likely to index heavily on existing designs. Mononoke is open source and in every LLM’s training set. If you ask Opus 5.5 or GPT-6 Astra (thanks Matthew Fowle ) about prior art, they both immediately point out the similarities to Mononoke. Giving credit to those that came before us is now easier — and more important — than ever. There is no longer an excuse. For an example of a system with similar insights but many key design differences, see Vicent Marti’s blog post for Cursor . ↩︎ Read other posts iddqd, or the hardest kind of unsafe Rust →

items.articleText: main Branches Tags Go to file Code Open more actions menu Latest commit History 748 Commits 748 Commits Folders and files Name Name Last commit message Last commit date .claude/ skills .claude/ skills .github .github cmd cmd docker docker docs docs internal internal itest itest scripts scripts web web .editorconfig .editorconfig .gitignore .gitignore .golangci.yml .golangci.yml AGENTS.md AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md CLAUDE.md CONTRIBUTING.md CONTRIBUTING.md LICENSE LICENSE Makefile Makefile README.md README.md SECURITY.md SECURITY.md go.mod go.mod go.sum go.sum View all files Repository files navigation Your Claude Code loops, working together and keeping you in the conversation. Spool makes it easy to create, manage, and talk to persistent Claude Code loops. Give them work, let them coordinate, and stay involved through chat. spool-demo.mp4 What does Spool make easier? Keep work going. Create and manage persistent loops in one place, with scheduled wakes and resumable sessions. Stay involved. Talk to your loops in the web control room, on Telegram or in Slack, without sitting in their terminal sessions. Coordinate work. Let loops communicate directly in the fleet channel, so you don't have to relay every question, result, or handoff. Less switching between sessions and carrying messages between loops. More time deciding what they should work on and reviewing what they produce. Spool is pre-1.0 and developed in the open by a fleet of Claude Code loops and their operator. The four loops in this repo's issues and PRs run on Spool, building Spool. Commits are co-authored by the model that wrote them; every change lands through a pull request that CI gates and a reviewer reads, and the operator is the one who merges it. Found a problem? CONTRIBUTING.md says how to report it and who answers. Quick start You need Linux, macOS or Windows with WSL2 , with Docker running, git , Go 1.25+, Node 20.19+ or 22.12+, and Claude Code on a Claude subscription (only to make a token in step 3). Get Spool and build it. git clone https://github.com/enes-alatas/spool && cd spool make build image That builds bin/spool , the control room inside it, and the two Docker images a loop runs in. Start it and sign in. Run ./bin/spool . On its first start it prints a one-time password for the user admin . Open http://127.0.0.1:8080 , sign in as admin with that password, and choose your own. Missed the password? ./bin/spool user reset admin prints a new one. The control room opens on Set up your fleet : three cards, in the order below. Each checks itself and turns done on its own. Harness. Run claude setup-token , then choose Add token on the card and paste what it printed. Your loops run on your Claude plan through it. Loops. Choose New loop , and give it a name and a mission. Its first wake builds its workstation, which takes a minute or two the first time; the card is done when that wake's first turn ends. Chat surface. Choose Attach a bot , then Attach Telegram or Attach Slack . Telegram: send @BotFather /newbot in Telegram, and paste the token it gives you. Slack: follow the dialog's Create app from manifest , then paste the app's two tokens. docs/SLACK.md has the steps. Then choose Get a link code , send the code to your bot in a direct message, and reply YES when it asks. That links your account and makes you the loop's owner. Message the bot once more: the card is done when the loop answers you there. No chat app? You can talk to a loop on its page in the control room instead. Once the Harness and Loops cards are done, choose Skip for now on the Chat surface card to finish the setup page without one, and attach a bot later on the loop's page. Other ways to run it From a release, once there is one after v0.5.1: it carries the built binary and the images, so you need no Go, Node or make . OPERATIONS.md shows the download, the checksum and the image pulls. On a server, as a service, with TLS and backups: OPERATIONS.md . Without Docker. ./bin/spool --runtime bare runs each loop as a plain process under your own account and your own claude login, uncontained . It needs no make image and no step 3. Read What contains a loop before you choose that. How it works Plain claude CLI underneath. Loops are claude subprocesses speaking stream-json over stdin/stdout. Your normal Claude Code login, plan and session limits apply. No API keys, no SDK. Direct coordination. Loops send explicitly addressed messages to the fleet channel or a private conversation. @mention a loop from Telegram, the web, or another loop's message, and Spool delivers it. Final turn replies stay as status notes in the timeline. Loop-to-loop chains are storm-guarded. Wake, sleep and pacing. Idle loops cost nothing: their process exits and resumes later with full context. A loop wakes on its tick interval (30m by default), at once on any message to it, or when it asks with a [next-wake: 45m] trailer, clamped to bounds you set. Paused loops queue their mail. Control room. The hub's web UI, at http://localhost:8080 by default. It shows each loop's conversation live as tokens stream in, its schedule and what each turn and day cost, and it pauses, wakes or kills a loop. Plan guardrails. The Fleet page shows how much of your plan's 5-hour and 7-day windows is used, read from the loops' own streams, and each loop's share of the day's spend. Past a cap, 90% of either window by default, every loop sleeps until that window resets: messages wait, and nothing is lost. Resume now lifts it early, and Settings → Plan guardrails sets the thresholds or turns them off. Security in brief Contained by default. Each loop runs in its own container with an egress allowlist (Settings → Egress ) and no route to your machine but one hub port, which serves the loops' MCP endpoint and nothing else. Uncontained only when you ask. Loops run with permission prompts bypassed. Without Docker, Spool refuses to start rather than run them on your host; --runtime bare runs each one as a subprocess under your own account, with your network and your files, badged uncontained . Signed in. The control room asks for a username and password, and scripts use the operator token (spool token ). Binding to localhost is not a boundary on its own. Secrets sealed. Bot tokens, connection secrets and the setup-token are sealed under hub.key in the data directory. Back it up apart from spool.db . docs/CONTAINMENT.md has the whole picture, including what containment does not do. SECURITY.md says how to report a vulnerability. Chat surfaces A loop starts with the control room only. Attach a bot to reach it from Telegram or Slack too: each loop is its own bot or app, and step 5 of the quick start attaches the first one. docs/TELEGRAM.md covers BotFather, groups and reactions; docs/SLACK.md covers the app manifest, the two tokens, reactions and polls. Who can talk to your loops Spool keeps a sender allowlist , and only people on it reach your loops. Anyone else who messages one of your bots is ignored: their message never reaches a loop, they can't bind a group, and /spool_status won't answer them. Linking your account in step 5 put you on it. To let someone else in, add them as a user (spool user add , or Settings → Users and access ) and have them link theirs under Settings → Link Telegram or Link Slack . Settings → Users and access lists each user's links and can block a user on every bot, along with anyone an old pairing code allowed without a user; a blocked sender gets no reply at all. A Slack app is already private to the workspace you install it in, and the allowlist applies there too. Loop-to-loop traffic is internal and unaffected. Flags Flag Default What it sets --listen 127.0.0.1:8080 where the control room and its API are served --data-dir ~/.spool the database, hub.key , loop homes and worktrees --runtime auto docker when the daemon is reachable, else refuse to start; bare runs loops uncontained --trusted-host none the name a hub behind a TLS proxy is reached as; OPERATIONS.md has a systemd unit and a Caddy recipe --mcp-listen chosen by the hub the loops' one port; docs/CONTAINMENT.md says how it is chosen spool --help lists every flag. spool token prints the operator token again. Development make server # Go binary only (uses last-built UI) make dev # run backend on :8080 make ui-dev # vite dev server with /api proxy make test # tier 1: unit + architecture tests make itest # tier 2: real binary vs fakeclaude (protocol fake), ~10min # (~7min without a docker daemon; two files skip) make image # build the spool-workstation and spool-egress images locally make lint # gofmt + vet (as Linux and as macOS) + golangci-lint make e2e-m1 # tier 3: real claude sessions (spends plan tokens) Testing is three-tiered (see docs/QUALITY.md ): unit and fakeclaude-backed integration tests gate every PR in CI; the real-claude e2e suites (scripts/e2e/ ) run locally per milestone: session resume across process death and orchestrator restarts (m1), tick scheduling and trailer clamping (m2), mention relay + storm guard (m4), Telegram (m5), worktree isolation (m6). Each in its own container, on your own plan without API costs. items.articleText:
## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.105.1
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.105.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.105.1
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

---

items.summary: Timken combines the expertise of Cone Drive, SPINEA, CGI Motion, and Timken Encoders to develop application-specific motion systems. The post Timken Precision Drives puts the motion challenge first in humanoid robots appeared first on The Robot Report .
items.articleText: Timken Precision Drives offers a portfolio of motion technologies for humanoid developers. Source: Timken, Shutterstock What does your humanoid robot’s motion system need to do? For engineers developing humanoids , the answer involves balancing torque, speed, stiffness, weight, positioning accuracy, and available space. Each joint presents its own requirements, and the right solution begins with understanding those demands. That is the approach behind Timken Precision Drives, part of The Timken Co. Bringing together Cone Drive , SPINEA, CGI Motion, and Timken Encoders, the platform combines specialized engineering expertise and complementary technologies to help customers solve their motion control challenges. The conversation starts with the application: What motion is required? What loads must the system support? Where is the current design falling short? And what needs to change to achieve the desired performance? Timken engineers around the application Developers of humanoids face different challenges across load-bearing joints, compact wrists, end effectors , and other moving assemblies. A system that meets the needs of one mechanism may require a different approach elsewhere in the robot. Timken Precision Drives said it works with customers to evaluate those requirements and identify an appropriate path forward. That may involve a standard component, a modified design, or a custom solution that brings multiple technologies together. Understanding the application early allows engineering teams to consider how gearing, motors , bearings, and position feedback will interact within the available space. It also helps guide decisions about reduction ratio, load capacity, allowable deflection, duty cycle, and service life. Register now and help us celebrate 20 years of RoboBusiness! Complementary technologies, custom possibilities Timken said its platform’s breadth gives engineers multiple ways to approach a motion challenge. Cone Drive contributes strain wave gearing expertise for applications requiring compact packaging, high torque density, and zero-backlash positioning. Component and housed configurations provide a foundation for application-specific designs, with opportunities to explore further integration based on customer requirements. SPINEA brings cycloidal gearing and integrated actuation expertise. TwinSpin reducers and DriveSpin servo actuators offer options for applications where torsional stiffness, torque transmission, and load-handling capability are important design considerations. CGI Motion adds precision planetary and micro gearing, along with custom design and manufacturing capabilities for compact mechanisms. That expertise supports the exploration of motion solutions where size, configuration, and performance requirements call for a tailored approach. Timken Encoders complements the mechanical portfolio with magnetic position feedback technologies , including absolute and incremental options. Timken Precision Drives said these combined capabilities enable it to look across technologies as it works with customers to develop solutions around their specific motion requirements. Timken’s platform brings together motion technologies from multiple units. Source: Timken Precision Drives Collaboration from concept through production Custom development begins with a clear understanding of the problem, according to Timken. A customer may need to reduce the size of an assembly, improve positioning accuracy, increase stiffness, or integrate feedback into an existing design. Timken Precision Drives said it brings application engineering and specialized product expertise into those discussions, supported by Timken’s global engineering and manufacturing resources. The goal is to work alongside the customer to determine which combination of technologies and design choices best addresses the application, whether refining an existing mechanism or developing something new. items.articleText: Across industries, the U.K. is putting the full stack to work. T he scale of deployment is growing fast, from enterprises transforming their businesses to startups solving some of the planet’s hardest problems. NVIDIA is putting that principle into practice, including through a five-year, $250 million compute commitment to strengthen the U.K.’s agentic safety and security research. NVIDIA’s Investments in the UK NVIDIA has been investing in the U.K. startup ecosystem, supporting companies including Basecamp Research , Ineffable Intelligence , Synthesia , Wayve and many more. Today, NVIDIA announced new planned investments in Boltz , Foresight , Hiverge, Prima Mente and Riverlane . Boltz , a London-based AI startup founded by MIT researchers, builds biomolecular models and AI agents that help scientists predict molecular structures and interactions, and design potential new medicines. Foresight, a London-based startup, helps owners of major infrastructure projects, including hyperscale data centers, predict completion dates, mitigate risks and accelerate time to revenue. Hiverge , a Cambridge-based AI startup founded by researchers from Google DeepMind and the University of Cambridge, builds an AI discovery engine that automatically writes and optimizes algorithms for tasks such as faster AI training and complex logistics planning. Prima Mente , a London-based AI biology startup, focuses on building biological foundation models to decode complex diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets, starting with Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and ALS. Riverlane, a Cambridge-based quantum computing startup, builds real-time error correction hardware and software that work across all major qubit types, helping quantum computers become reliable enough for practical use. In addition, NVIDIA is partnering with the Earthshot Prize , joining as a Global Alliance Founding Partner to bring compute and technical expertise to innovators working on solutions for the world’s greatest climate and sustainability challenges. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Technology Leaders Pioneer Intelligent Solutions Across the UK In energy, Fuse Energy is moving its customer AI onto its own in-house infrastructure, built on NVIDIA B300 Blackwell Ultra, delivering faster, more responsive support to over 450,000 U.K. households. Meanwhile, sovereign AI company Locai Labs released Nemotron-Personas-UK — an open source dataset of one million synthetic personas representing the UK’s demographic, regional and cultural diversity — helping developers build fairer, more representative AI systems. Healthcare In healthcare, OneAdvanced is deploying what it calls the U.K.’s first and most advanced fine-tuned LLM for Primary Care AI-triage — built with NVIDIA Agent Toolkit software and open models — supporting millions of National Health Service patients. Heidi has now integrated NVIDIA Nemotron open models to give clinicians faster access to trusted medical evidence. Speechmatics is deploying Oak, a multilingual medical speech recognition model, using NVIDIA Triton Inference — giving healthcare organizations control over where sensitive patient audio is processed. Apian , Synnovis and NVIDIA are teaming up to use advanced computing and digital simulations using NVIDIA Cosmos to help hospital robots handle the heavy lifting of moving lab samples, freeing up medical staff to focus on patient care. Danaher and NVIDIA are collaborating to advance autonomous science and help accelerate the pace of discovery by bringing accelerated computing, scientific and physical AI into laboratory workflows and instruments. Danaher’s recently announced AI-powered autonomous lab — designed to deliver up to 8x faster discovery of affinity reagents — is using NVIDIA BioNeMo open models within its AI-driven protein design workflows, data and automation technologies that connect design with experimental feedback. Smart Cities On the civic side, Liverpool City Region is building an NVIDIA-powered “City Brain” — a sovereign AI strategy designed as a blueprint for dozens of Unitary Authorities across the U.K. Digital Jersey , Innovation City Belfast and Tees Valley Combined Authority are each exploring how trusted AI compute can serve communities and public services. Financial Services In financial services, LSEG and NVIDIA are bringing GPU-accelerated market analytics to global institutions. Revolut introduced PRAGMA earlier in the year — a foundation model for banking event sequences, pre-trained on 26 million anonymised user histories. PRAGMA has moved from research to real-time scaling. Lloyds Banking Group built ATUM , a transaction foundation model that converts billions of banking transactions into reusable AI. And Starling is developing a banking foundation model trained on Civo’s U.K. sovereign cloud infrastructure. NatWest is collaborating with NVIDIA on Nemotron Voice to better understand how banking customers across the U.K. speak, while Modulr is deploying a network of agents using Nemotron for distinct parts of payment operations. Quantum Quantum is moving from research to systems deployable alongside classical AI, and the U.K. is at the heart of this shift. Riverlane has shown how GPUs can accelerate decoder recalibration workflows used in quantum error correction, helping decoder performance keep pace with real-time changes in quantum hardware behaviour. The work forms part of a broader collaboration exploring how AI, accelerated computing and quantum error-correction technologies can work together to support future quantum systems. Together, these announcements showcase how enterprises, organizations and startups in the U.K. are fostering innovation across the nation. This includes more than 3,100 U.K. companies that are a part of the NVIDIA Inception program for cutting-edge startups. Tune in to NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s GTC Berlin keynote on Wednesday, Oct. 21, at 11 a.m. CEST. items.articleText: Keeping a city running means making decisions that affect residents every day — from when to repair a road to how to use energy more efficiently. Across the EMEA region, cities and local software, infrastructure and integration partners are using NVIDIA accelerated computing to build physical AI agents and digital twins that help teams make those decisions. These applications can anticipate maintenance needs, guide urban planning and make public services more responsive. Software partners including ABA Technology , Akila , Galene AI , Honeywell Technologies , K2K , Linker Vision , Milestone , Onetera , ThinkDeep and Younite AI are using NVIDIA physical and agentic AI to develop solutions for city operations and public services. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/linker-vision.mp4 Video courtesy of Linker Vision. NVIDIA Cosmos open models and the NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) help agents interpret video and identify conditions, such as traffic congestion, equipment condition, underused spaces and safety hazards, that need attention. NVIDIA Nemotron open models enable developers to build agents that reason over information, respond in natural language and deploy digital twins with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Projects span Belgium, Finland, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Sweden, the U.K. and elsewhere. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements In the U.K., the Liverpool City Region , K2K is exploring how to build AI factories using NVIDIA accelerated computing, Cosmos and the VSS blueprint that can support urban planning and public services — testing applications for mobility and safety. The Island of Jersey is working with K2K to strengthen decision-making, mobility and urban planning while advancing clean energy and public services. Innovation City Belfast is exploring a pilot with K2K focused on smart mobility, transport systems, citizen safety and event and response management. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/IKM®-�-Video-GTC-V.10.10.2-compressed.mp4 Video courtesy of K2K. In France, the Department of Côte-d’Or , Akila and ThinkDeep built operations agents that combine sensor, infrastructure and historical data in a sovereign digital twin using NVIDIA Nemotron, Omniverse and accelerated computing, with Cosmos adoption planned for video data. Across more than 500 public buildings, the agents support energy, compliance, safety and climate resilience, and cut document search time from weeks to minutes and reduce total operating costs by 10%, targeting 30% at scale. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Akila-CGCO-compressed.mp4 Video courtesy of Akila. In addition, Port Sud de France in Sète is working with ThinkDeep’s agentic platform that uses Cosmos and Nemotron to analyze cargo and safety data, coordinate operations and guide secure handling of hazardous materials. In Italy’s Milan region, Galene.AI , Dell Technologies and TD Synnex are deploying an NVIDIA-powered, locally operated AI factory, starting with Cinisello Balsamo and planning expansion to four additional municipalities. Services include real-time translation, citizen chatbots and assistance with procurement and funding. These applications aim to simplify administrative work and help people get access to municipal data in seconds versus hours, while keeping local governance of data. At Belgium’s Port of Antwerp-Bruges , Milestone and Dell Technologies are testing how agentic vision AI technologies, using NVIDIA Cosmos and the VSS blueprint, could support complex use cases such as oil-spill warnings by training models with synthetic data to prepare for incidents where real-world data is scarce. In the Nordics, Younite AI is developing a digital twin experience with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for Gothenburg in Sweden as a part of the EU’s Citiverse initiative, focused on helping cities simulate changes and improve accessibility by providing event entrance previews, seating and crowd conditions before arrival. These cities point toward a broader ambition: adapting agentic applications to local needs and extending them across departments and neighboring municipalities and countries such as Poland’s city of Wroclaw. Elsewhere in the region, Honeywell Technologies is deploying Forge Cognition, powered by NVIDIA Nemotron, Cosmos, Omniverse and the VSS blueprint, at the Dubai Fairmont Hotel to connect AI agents with building systems and improve reliability, energy efficiency and operations. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/honeywell.mp4 Video courtesy of Honeywell Technologies. Building the AI Infrastructure for European Cities For European cities, scaling from pilots to everyday operations requires infrastructure that can process local data, customize models and run AI agents. System builders and infrastructure partners including Cisco , Dell Technologies , HPE , Lenovo and Supermicro are packaging NVIDIA accelerated computing, networking and storage into locally operated AI factories. These systems let cities customize and run intelligent applications locally while retaining control of their data, models and operations. Nebius and Net Zero Compute are part of the broader ecosystem building AI factories designed to accelerate deployment and reduce costs for agentic services. EY and Accenture provide the integration and operational expertise to connect applications with city systems. Their work helps cities build repeatable deployment blueprints that they can adapt across departments and expand as local needs grow. Learn how NVIDIA and its ecosystem are bringing physical AI, agentic AI and local AI factories to cities worldwide at Smart City Expo World Congress , running Nov. 3-5 in Barcelona. entries.title: ros2_pulse, rclpy 노드 계측 및 대여 메시지(loaned messages) 측정 기능 추가
entries.reason: ROS 2 환경에서 토픽 빈도 및 노드 활성 상태를 모니터링하는 진단 도구의 파이썬 노드 및 대여 메시지 지원 세부 사항을 다룸

facts.statement: ros2_pulse는 LD_PRELOAD 기반 프로브로 rmw_take 추적 지점을 후킹하여 rclpy 및 rclc 수신을 계측하며, 대여 메시지(loaned messages)를 별도 측정하고 Prometheus 및 Grafana 연동을 지원한다.
facts.quote: The probe now also hooks the rmw_take tracepoint, so rclpy (and rclc) receives count too.

entries.title: 지속형 Claude Code 루프 오케스트레이션 도구 Spool 공개
entries.reason: Claude Code 세션을 도커 컨테이너 격리 환경에서 지속형 에이전트로 관리하고 메신저와 연동하는 실무 도구 정보를 제공함

facts.statement: Spool은 지속적인 Claude Code 다중 에이전트 루프를 생성 및 관리하고 웹 제어실, Slack, Telegram을 통해 조율할 수 있도록 지원하는 오픈소스 도구다.
facts.quote: Spool makes it easy to create, manage, and talk to persistent Claude Code loops.

entries.title: Anthropic Python SDK v1.14.0 릴리스
entries.reason: OpenTelemetry 추적 지원 및 관리형 에이전트 식별자 등 최신 API 기능 변경 사항을 전달함

facts.statement: Anthropic Python SDK v1.14.0에서 API 호출, 스트리밍, 도구 실행에 대한 OpenTelemetry 트레이싱 지원이 추가되고 관리형 에이전트에 execution_identity 필드가 도입되었다.
facts.quote: add OpenTelemetry tracing for API calls, streaming and tool runs

entries.title: Ollama v0.40.4, CLI 의사결정 모델 실행 및 llama-server 멀티모달 임베딩 지원
entries.reason: 로컬 LLM 런타임의 CLI 의사결정 모델 실행 기능 및 멀티모달 임베딩 등 기능 개선 내역을 다룸

facts.statement: Ollama v0.40.4는 터미널 CLI에서 ollama run을 통해 의사결정 모델을 직접 실행할 수 있게 지원하며, llama-server를 통한 멀티모달 임베딩 지원 및 Apple 실리콘 MLX 러너 성능이 개선되었다.
facts.quote: Decision models can now be used directly from the terminal with ollama run

entries.title: NVIDIA, 영국 스타트업 신규 투자 및 2억 5천만 달러 컴퓨팅 지원 발표
entries.reason: AI 인프라 및 스타트업 생태계 대상 대규모 컴퓨팅 투자와 전략적 스타트업 투자 내역을 다룸

facts.statement: NVIDIA는 영국 에이전틱 안전 및 보안 연구를 위한 5년간 2억 5,000만 달러 규모의 컴퓨팅 지원과 함께 Boltz, Foresight, Hiverge, Prima Mente, Riverlane 등 영국 스타트업에 대한 신규 투자 계획을 발표했다.
facts.quote: NVIDIA announced new planned investments in Boltz , Foresight , Hiverge, Prima Mente and Riverlane .

omitted.reason: 재단 내부 일정 및 행사 후속 작업에 대한 일반 주간 회고로 구체적인 기술 성과가 부족함

특정 지역의 인턴십 채용 공고로 기술 개발 및 산업 동향 기준에 미달함
한 줄 요약 피드 수준의 마케팅성 고객 사례로 구체적인 기술 세부 정보가 부족함
한 줄 요약 피드 수준의 도입 사례 홍보로 구체적인 기술 설명이 없음
한 줄 요약 피드 수준의 사례 소개로 기술적 재현성 및 세부 근거가 부족함
버전 관리 시스템 아키텍처에 대한 개인 블로그 논평 및 표절 의혹 제기로 기술적 도구 정보에 미달함
상세 설명 없이 특정 PR 번호만 나열된 단순 패치 백포트 릴리스임
컨퍼런스 패널 토의 및 행사 일정 홍보 기사로 제외 대상에 해당함
기업의 부품 포트폴리오 홍보 및 전시회 참가 안내 성격의 기사임
여러 유럽 도시의 디지털 트윈 파일럿 사례를 나열한 기업 홍보성 모음 기사로 핵심 변화의 구체성이 낮음

Python nodes are counted on both sides now. Before, a Python subscriber’s deliveries never showed up, because rclpy isn’t instrumented. The probe now also hooks the rmw_take tracepoint, so rclpy (and rclc) receives count too. rclcpp still counts at callback_start , so nothing is counted twice. selectedItems.articleText: main Branches Tags Go to file Code Open more actions menu Latest commit History 748 Commits 748 Commits Folders and files Name Name Last commit message Last commit date .claude/ skills .claude/ skills .github .github cmd cmd docker docker docs docs internal internal itest itest scripts scripts web web .editorconfig .editorconfig .gitignore .gitignore .golangci.yml .golangci.yml AGENTS.md AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md CLAUDE.md CONTRIBUTING.md CONTRIBUTING.md LICENSE LICENSE Makefile Makefile README.md README.md SECURITY.md SECURITY.md go.mod go.mod go.sum go.sum View all files Repository files navigation Your Claude Code loops, working together and keeping you in the conversation. Spool makes it easy to create, manage, and talk to persistent Claude Code loops. Give them work, let them coordinate, and stay involved through chat. spool-demo.mp4 What does Spool make easier? Keep work going. Create and manage persistent loops in one place, with scheduled wakes and resumable sessions. Stay involved. Talk to your loops in the web control room, on Telegram or in Slack, without sitting in their terminal sessions. Coordinate work. Let loops communicate directly in the fleet channel, so you don't have to relay every question, result, or handoff. Less switching between sessions and carrying messages between loops. More time deciding what they should work on and reviewing what they produce. Spool is pre-1.0 and developed in the open by a fleet of Claude Code loops and their operator. The four loops in this repo's issues and PRs run on Spool, building Spool. Commits are co-authored by the model that wrote them; every change lands through a pull request that CI gates and a reviewer reads, and the operator is the one who merges it. Found a problem? CONTRIBUTING.md says how to report it and who answers. Quick start You need Linux, macOS or Windows with WSL2 , with Docker running, git , Go 1.25+, Node 20.19+ or 22.12+, and Claude Code on a Claude subscription (only to make a token in step 3). Get Spool and build it. git clone https://github.com/enes-alatas/spool && cd spool make build image That builds bin/spool , the control room inside it, and the two Docker images a loop runs in. Start it and sign in. Run ./bin/spool . On its first start it prints a one-time password for the user admin . Open http://127.0.0.1:8080 , sign in as admin with that password, and choose your own. Missed the password? ./bin/spool user reset admin prints a new one. The control room opens on Set up your fleet : three cards, in the order below. Each checks itself and turns done on its own. Harness. Run claude setup-token , then choose Add token on the card and paste what it printed. Your loops run on your Claude plan through it. Loops. Choose New loop , and give it a name and a mission. Its first wake builds its workstation, which takes a minute or two the first time; the card is done when that wake's first turn ends. Chat surface. Choose Attach a bot , then Attach Telegram or Attach Slack . Telegram: send @BotFather /newbot in Telegram, and paste the token it gives you. Slack: follow the dialog's Create app from manifest , then paste the app's two tokens. docs/SLACK.md has the steps. Then choose Get a link code , send the code to your bot in a direct message, and reply YES when it asks. That links your account and makes you the loop's owner. Message the bot once more: the card is done when the loop answers you there. No chat app? You can talk to a loop on its page in the control room instead. Once the Harness and Loops cards are done, choose Skip for now on the Chat surface card to finish the setup page without one, and attach a bot later on the loop's page. Other ways to run it From a release, once there is one after v0.5.1: it carries the built binary and the images, so you need no Go, Node or make . OPERATIONS.md shows the download, the checksum and the image pulls. On a server, as a service, with TLS and backups: OPERATIONS.md . Without Docker. ./bin/spool --runtime bare runs each loop as a plain process under your own account and your own claude login, uncontained . It needs no make image and no step 3. Read What contains a loop before you choose that. How it works Plain claude CLI underneath. Loops are claude subprocesses speaking stream-json over stdin/stdout. Your normal Claude Code login, plan and session limits apply. No API keys, no SDK. Direct coordination. Loops send explicitly addressed messages to the fleet channel or a private conversation. @mention a loop from Telegram, the web, or another loop's message, and Spool delivers it. Final turn replies stay as status notes in the timeline. Loop-to-loop chains are storm-guarded. Wake, sleep and pacing. Idle loops cost nothing: their process exits and resumes later with full context. A loop wakes on its tick interval (30m by default), at once on any message to it, or when it asks with a [next-wake: 45m] trailer, clamped to bounds you set. Paused loops queue their mail. Control room. The hub's web UI, at http://localhost:8080 by default. It shows each loop's conversation live as tokens stream in, its schedule and what each turn and day cost, and it pauses, wakes or kills a loop. Plan guardrails. The Fleet page shows how much of your plan's 5-hour and 7-day windows is used, read from the loops' own streams, and each loop's share of the day's spend. Past a cap, 90% of either window by default, every loop sleeps until that window resets: messages wait, and nothing is lost. Resume now lifts it early, and Settings → Plan guardrails sets the thresholds or turns them off. Security in brief Contained by default. Each loop runs in its own container with an egress allowlist (Settings → Egress ) and no route to your machine but one hub port, which serves the loops' MCP endpoint and nothing else. Uncontained only when you ask. Loops run with permission prompts bypassed. Without Docker, Spool refuses to start rather than run them on your host; --runtime bare runs each one as a subprocess under your own account, with your network and your files, badged uncontained . Signed in. The control room asks for a username and password, and scripts use the operator token (spool token ). Binding to localhost is not a boundary on its own. Secrets sealed. Bot tokens, connection secrets and the setup-token are sealed under hub.key in the data directory. Back it up apart from spool.db . docs/CONTAINMENT.md has the whole picture, including what containment does not do. SECURITY.md says how to report a vulnerability. Chat surfaces A loop starts with the control room only. Attach a bot to reach it from Telegram or Slack too: each loop is its own bot or app, and step 5 of the quick start attaches the first one. docs/TELEGRAM.md covers BotFather, groups and reactions; docs/SLACK.md covers the app manifest, the two tokens, reactions and polls. Who can talk to your loops Spool keeps a sender allowlist , and only people on it reach your loops. Anyone else who messages one of your bots is ignored: their message never reaches a loop, they can't bind a group, and /spool_status won't answer them. Linking your account in step 5 put you on it. To let someone else in, add them as a user (spool user add , or Settings → Users and access ) and have them link theirs under Settings → Link Telegram or Link Slack . Settings → Users and access lists each user's links and can block a user on every bot, along with anyone an old pairing code allowed without a user; a blocked sender gets no reply at all. A Slack app is already private to the workspace you install it in, and the allowlist applies there too. Loop-to-loop traffic is internal and unaffected. Flags Flag Default What it sets --listen 127.0.0.1:8080 where the control room and its API are served --data-dir ~/.spool the database, hub.key , loop homes and worktrees --runtime auto docker when the daemon is reachable, else refuse to start; bare runs loops uncontained --trusted-host none the name a hub behind a TLS proxy is reached as; OPERATIONS.md has a systemd unit and a Caddy recipe --mcp-listen chosen by the hub the loops' one port; docs/CONTAINMENT.md says how it is chosen spool --help lists every flag. spool token prints the operator token again. Development make server # Go binary only (uses last-built UI) make dev # run backend on :8080 make ui-dev # vite dev server with /api proxy make test # tier 1: unit + architecture tests make itest # tier 2: real binary vs fakeclaude (protocol fake), ~10min # (~7min without a docker daemon; two files skip) make image # build the spool-workstation and spool-egress images locally make lint # gofmt + vet (as Linux and as macOS) + golangci-lint make e2e-m1 # tier 3: real claude sessions (spends plan tokens) Testing is three-tiered (see docs/QUALITY.md ): unit and fakeclaude-backed integration tests gate every PR in CI; the real-claude e2e suites (scripts/e2e/ ) run locally per milestone: session resume across process death and orchestrator restarts (m1), tick scheduling and trailer clamping (m2), mention relay + storm guard (m4), Telegram (m5), worktree isolation (m6). Project docs Running a hub: docs/OPERATIONS.md : install on a server, back up, restore and upgrade docs/CONTAINMENT.md : what contains a loop, and the hub's own secrets docs/TELEGRAM.md , docs/SLACK.md : the chat surfaces in full SECURITY.md : what is supported, how to report a vulnerability privately, and which properties of the design are known rather than bugs Working on Spool: CONTRIBUTING.md : how to report a problem and who answers docs/VISION.md : product vision and the L0–L7 milestone ladder docs/ARCHITECTURE.md : shape, seams, ubiquitous language docs/CONVENTIONS.md : workflow, style, test tiers docs/QUALITY.md : baselines and CI gates docs/THREAT-MODEL.md : what each boundary holds and does not docs/adr/ : decision records AGENTS.md : orientation for AI agents working on this repo (CLAUDE.md is a symlink to it) About fleet of persistent Claude Code coworkers you talk to in Telegram and Slack. Each in its own container, on your own plan without API costs. ## Decision models in the CLI
Decision models can now be used directly from the terminal with `ollama run` — ask yes/no questions, classify text into labels, or score against a rubric:
`ollama run nimble --ask "Is a refund being requested?" < ticket.txt`

 ## What's Changed
  * Kev decision models are now supported by the MLX runner on Apple silicon
  * `ollama launch` can now be used with usage credits without upgrading to a paid plan
  * `ollama launch codex` now includes locally installed Ollama models in its model picker. Use `/model` within the Codex CLI to swap models.

  * Fixed loading multimodal embedding models with small context windows

  * MLX runner now clips long Laya states instead of rejecting them

selectedItems.articleText: Across industries, the U.K. is putting the full stack to work. T he scale of deployment is growing fast, from enterprises transforming their businesses to startups solving some of the planet’s hardest problems. NVIDIA is putting that principle into practice, including through a five-year, $250 million compute commitment to strengthen the U.K.’s agentic safety and security research. NVIDIA’s Investments in the UK NVIDIA has been investing in the U.K. startup ecosystem, supporting companies including Basecamp Research , Ineffable Intelligence , Synthesia , Wayve and many more. Today, NVIDIA announced new planned investments in Boltz , Foresight , Hiverge, Prima Mente and Riverlane . Boltz , a London-based AI startup founded by MIT researchers, builds biomolecular models and AI agents that help scientists predict molecular structures and interactions, and design potential new medicines. Foresight, a London-based startup, helps owners of major infrastructure projects, including hyperscale data centers, predict completion dates, mitigate risks and accelerate time to revenue. Hiverge , a Cambridge-based AI startup founded by researchers from Google DeepMind and the University of Cambridge, builds an AI discovery engine that automatically writes and optimizes algorithms for tasks such as faster AI training and complex logistics planning. Prima Mente , a London-based AI biology startup, focuses on building biological foundation models to decode complex diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets, starting with Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and ALS. Riverlane, a Cambridge-based quantum computing startup, builds real-time error correction hardware and software that work across all major qubit types, helping quantum computers become reliable enough for practical use. In addition, NVIDIA is partnering with the Earthshot Prize , joining as a Global Alliance Founding Partner to bring compute and technical expertise to innovators working on solutions for the world’s greatest climate and sustainability challenges. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Technology Leaders Pioneer Intelligent Solutions Across the UK In energy, Fuse Energy is moving its customer AI onto its own in-house infrastructure, built on NVIDIA B300 Blackwell Ultra, delivering faster, more responsive support to over 450,000 U.K. households. Meanwhile, sovereign AI company Locai Labs released Nemotron-Personas-UK — an open source dataset of one million synthetic personas representing the UK’s demographic, regional and cultural diversity — helping developers build fairer, more representative AI systems. Healthcare In healthcare, OneAdvanced is deploying what it calls the U.K.’s first and most advanced fine-tuned LLM for Primary Care AI-triage — built with NVIDIA Agent Toolkit software and open models — supporting millions of National Health Service patients. Heidi has now integrated NVIDIA Nemotron open models to give clinicians faster access to trusted medical evidence. Speechmatics is deploying Oak, a multilingual medical speech recognition model, using NVIDIA Triton Inference — giving healthcare organizations control over where sensitive patient audio is processed. Apian , Synnovis and NVIDIA are teaming up to use advanced computing and digital simulations using NVIDIA Cosmos to help hospital robots handle the heavy lifting of moving lab samples, freeing up medical staff to focus on patient care. Danaher and NVIDIA are collaborating to advance autonomous science and help accelerate the pace of discovery by bringing accelerated computing, scientific and physical AI into laboratory workflows and instruments. Danaher’s recently announced AI-powered autonomous lab — designed to deliver up to 8x faster discovery of affinity reagents — is using NVIDIA BioNeMo open models within its AI-driven protein design workflows, data and automation technologies that connect design with experimental feedback.
